newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer Dome sees output boost from plan.
newsitem.headline: Placer Dome sees output boost from plan.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc's plan to expand its Pipeline gold project in Nevada will significantly boost production levels and lower average costs for the gold company, Placer Dome's chief executive said in an interview on Tuesday.

"What you see here is a whole project, which goes for a long time, with an average output of 440,000 ounces per year and with a cash cost of around US$150 an ounce on average," John Willson told Reuters after a meeting with analysts.
"It's a very significant asset for Placer Dome."
The company said earlier today it planned to merge the 4.3 million-ounce Pipeline project with a newly explored property next door, the 2.5 million-ounce South Pipeline project.
The expansion will boost production to 440,000 ounces per year from 310,000 ounces a year for Pipeline alone and help lower company-wide cash costs, which now average about US$235 an ounce.
Production was expected to start in April 1997, three months ahead of schedule, Willson said. The project should be about $50 million under the $320 million budget, he added.
The mine has an expected life of 12 years, with production in the first five years being the highest, at about 575,000 ounces a year and average cash costs about US$114 an ounce.

The company should be producing 2.75 million ounces a year between 1998 and 2000, with new production from Pipeline and South Pipeline as well as expected output from the Musselwhite project in Northern Ontario and the Las Cristinas property in Venezuela, said Jay Taylor, president of Placer Dome U.S. Inc.
Placer expects to produce 1.95 million ounces in 1996.
"I like the growth profile going forward," said one analyst. "Costs are going to be very low."
The project is a joint venture 60 percent owned by Placer Dome and 40 percent owned by British-Australian mining conglomerate RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd .
The expansion proves Placer's strategy to replace dwindling reserves through its own exploration can work well, Willson said.
"This is a great example of the success of our strategy."
The Pipeline reserves cost between US$12 and US$13 an ounce to find, much less than the cost of acquiring reserves through acquisitions, he said.
But he would not rule out future acquisitions.
He said the company has looked seriously at acquiring part of Bre-X Minerals Ltd, whose spectacular Indonesian gold discovery has attracted interest from most of the world's major gold companies.
Placer Dome will decide on its next move after Bre-X outlines a bidding process, Willson said.
Bre-X has said it will look for a major gold producer to buy 25 percent of the Busang deposit.
